differentiation.3-4: Give child a pile of leaves. Ask them to put big ones here and small ones there. Show with hands.
differentiation.4-5: Sort leaves into three groups: big, medium, small. Count each group aloud.
differentiation.5-6: Sort by size AND by shape (round vs pointy). Write or draw the number in each group.

teacher_tip: Walk around and name each group. Do not correct — naming is the learning.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Use leaves with very different textures (smooth vs rough). Guide hands gently.
inclusion_adaptations.motor_delay: Provide a tray with raised edges so leaves don't scatter. Give more time.
inclusion_adaptations.stutter: Do not ask child to announce results aloud. A nod or pointing counts.
inclusion_adaptations.shy: Let child sort independently first, then show one peer when ready.

differentiation.3-4: Jump with both feet together on the spot 5 times. Clap for each jump.
differentiation.4-5: Hop on one foot 3 times, switch. Walk heel-to-toe along a chalk line.
differentiation.5-6: Hopscotch grid with 6 squares. Count each square. Lead the group.

teacher_tip: Start seated children clapping to keep them engaged while others move.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Hold hands for the heel-to-toe walk. Describe each step verbally.
inclusion_adaptations.shy: Pair with a trusted peer. Let them go together rather than alone.
inclusion_adaptations.stutter: No verbal performance required. Smiling and doing = full participation.

differentiation.3-4: Sort objects into two bowls: nature things vs non-nature things. Use a pebble as example.
differentiation.4-5: Sort by colour AND by material. Use three bowls.
differentiation.5-6: Create own sorting rule. Explain the rule to one peer.

teacher_tip: Never tell a child their sort is wrong. Ask: 'Why did you put it here?' to surface thinking.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Use objects with strong texture contrast. Guide exploration with touch.
inclusion_adaptations.motor_delay: Larger objects, wider bowls. Sort by pointing if picking up is hard.
inclusion_adaptations.stutter: Explain rule by pointing or drawing instead of speaking.

differentiation.3-4: Show a picture. Ask: 'What is this?' One word answers are fine. Repeat the word clearly.
differentiation.4-5: Show a picture. Ask: 'What is happening?' Encourage a full sentence.
differentiation.5-6: Three pictures in a row. Ask child to make a short story connecting all three.

teacher_tip: For shy children: let them whisper to you privately before sharing with the group.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Describe the picture aloud first. Ask child to imagine and respond.
inclusion_adaptations.stutter: Give extra wait time. Never finish sentences for them. A thumbs-up counts as participation.
inclusion_adaptations.shy: Start with private whisper. Graduate to pair share before group share.

differentiation.3-4: Count pebbles 1 to 5. Touch each one and say the number aloud.
differentiation.4-5: Count 1 to 10. Make two groups and say which has more.
differentiation.5-6: Add two groups together. Write the number in sand or on paper.

teacher_tip: Touch-counting is the key skill. Never rush. Let the child set the pace.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Large pebbles or stones, guided hand-over-hand counting.
inclusion_adaptations.motor_delay: Use a container. Child drops pebbles in one at a time, counts drops.
inclusion_adaptations.stutter: Counting aloud is optional. Pointing counts.

differentiation.3-4: Pass a pebble around the circle. Each child holds it for 3 seconds then passes. Smile at the person they pass to.
differentiation.4-5: Take turns completing one part of a drawing (sun, cloud, house, tree). Ask: 'What did your friend add?'
differentiation.5-6: Work in pairs to build the tallest twig tower. Discuss strategy before starting.

teacher_tip: Name the positive behaviour: 'Raju, you waited so patiently!' This is more powerful than correction.

inclusion_adaptations.shy: Let shy child start — being first removes the anxiety of waiting and watching.
inclusion_adaptations.stutter: No verbal turn required. Physical passing or nodding counts.
inclusion_adaptations.motor_delay: Seated in the circle. Adapted role: holds a special item (the 'score keeper' stone).

differentiation.3-4: Squeeze, roll, flatten clay freely. Name what you made after.
differentiation.4-5: Make a roti shape (flat circle) and a ball shape. Compare sizes.
differentiation.5-6: Make an animal or object using three pieces. Give it a name and tell one thing about it.

teacher_tip: Display every child's creation. Naming it on display is a powerful identity moment.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Fully tactile. Describe textures as child works. Let them feel others' creations.
inclusion_adaptations.motor_delay: Softer clay. Use palm press instead of finger pinch. Seat at a stable table.
inclusion_adaptations.shy: Work next to worker first. Sharing with group is optional.

differentiation.3-4: Tear paper into small pieces. Glue (or press with mud) onto a leaf outline.
differentiation.4-5: Fold paper in half and half again. Cut or tear a simple fringe.
differentiation.5-6: Create a leaf print by rubbing a pencil or chalk over a leaf under paper.

teacher_tip: Tearing paper builds the same pincer grip as writing. Frame it as art, not exercise.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Feel the leaf edges first. Focus on tearing and texture collage.
inclusion_adaptations.motor_delay: Pre-score paper for easier tearing. Wide crayon for rubbings.

differentiation.3-4: Tell a 3-sentence story with animal sounds. Ask: 'What sound did the cow make?'
differentiation.4-5: Tell a 5-sentence story. Ask children to repeat the last line together.
differentiation.5-6: Tell half a story. Ask a child to finish it. Accept any ending.

teacher_tip: Use local names and local animals in the story. Familiarity doubles engagement.

inclusion_adaptations.stutter: Answering with animal sounds (moo, baa) removes pressure of words.
inclusion_adaptations.shy: Whisper the animal sound to worker — no group performance needed.

differentiation.3-4: Give two identical leaves. Ask child to find the matching one from a pile of three.
differentiation.4-5: Match leaves by shape from a pile of six. Group identical ones together.
differentiation.5-6: Match shadow cards to objects. Describe why they match.

teacher_tip: Self-correction is the goal — not checking with the worker. Turn it away from you.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Match by texture or size instead of visual shape.
inclusion_adaptations.motor_delay: Point to match instead of picking up.

differentiation.3-4: Roll a ball (or pebble on a flat surface) back and forth with a partner.
differentiation.4-5: Throw a ball underarm to a partner 1 meter away. Count successful catches.
differentiation.5-6: Three-person passing in a triangle. Count without dropping.

teacher_tip: Every child should get at least 3 turns. Count turns, not just successes.

inclusion_adaptations.visual_impaired: Use a rustling ball or shake seeds in a tied cloth bag so sound guides catching.
inclusion_adaptations.shy: Start with worker as partner before child-to-child.
inclusion_adaptations.motor_delay: Seated rolling. Lower the distance to 50 cm.

differentiation.3-4: Say your name and one thing you like. Worker demonstrates first.
differentiation.4-5: Say your name and your friend's name next to you. Say one thing they did today.
differentiation.5-6: Introduce a friend to the group: name, age, one thing they are good at.

teacher_tip: This builds identity. Use it especially for children returning after absence.

inclusion_adaptations.stutter: Let the peer introduce the child with stutter, or let them hold up a picture they drew.
inclusion_adaptations.shy: Worker introduces the shy child first as a model. Participation is never forced.
